titulo: Project: a safe motion, end to end
lead: Each lesson left you one piece: clip read, retargeting with no violations, motion tracking measured, safety check. What goes to a robot is the whole chain, in a single movement. In this lesson you run the four steps in sequence, check that they all pass and refer to the same file, and generate your own study plan.
objetivo: run the chain mocap → retargeting → motion tracking → safety on a single motion and prove that all four steps pass.

aprende.t: Four safety rules read from the motion itself
The four-step chain and the file that ties them all together
The most common mistake: checking one motion and sending another
Your plan with dates for the next steps

hero_alt: Humanoid robot with a dark visor doing a slow arm motion inside a square marked with yellow tape, under a gantry, with a blurred technician holding a tablet.

nos.detalhe: The BVH, read and checked: frames, fps, complete lines. Writes etapas/1-clipe.json.
The same BVH taken to the G1 by GMR, with no frame outside the limit. Writes etapas/2-retarget.json with the name of the source BVH.

The motion played back in the simulator with the gantry: mean joint error and fall. In a real project, this is where the trained motion tracking policy goes (mjlab, SONIC), and the criterion is no gantry.

Joint limits, joint speed below a ceiling, feet not going through the floor, and pelvis inside the work area. The speed ceiling and the area radius are rules of your lab: the research behind the program does not give the G1's maximum speed per joint.

secoes.legenda: The chain only holds if steps 2, 3, and 4 talk about the same file and step 2 comes from the BVH in step 1.

Frames 1200 to 2400 pass retargeting and motion tracking, but the knee reaches 635°/s and the foot drops 1.9 cm below the standing pose (retargeting does not enforce ground contact). The chain closes on a single file and fails: that is the right result.

secoes.titulo: A batch of motions going through the chain
secoes.sub: Datasets like SONIC's have millions of frames: the chain runs as a queue. Run it, interrupt it halfway, and run it again.

msg.inicio: 3 motions in a conferir/. Click "Run the batch".
msg.rodando: One motion at a time: retargeting, motion tracking, and safety, and then aprovados/ or reprovados/.
msg.parou: Interrupted. The middle motion stayed in na cadeia/. Run again to see it resume.
msg.retoma: Resume: what was in the chain went back to a conferir/. What was already approved is not redone.
msg.fimfalha: Empty batch. The 1200–2400 segment went to reprovados/ with the reason (knee at 635°/s and foot below the floor): that's the one you review, without redoing the batch.

exercicios.texto: Run the full chain on the boxing motion. Before running it, on a fresh bench, the check shows the steps that are missing.

secoes.sub: The explanation appears after your answer.

perguntas.p: Each step passed on its own, but the check says "cadeia quebrada". What happened?
opcoes: GMR changed versions in the middle of the chain without telling the kit.
The simulator gave a different result on the second run.
The steps checked different motion files.
The source BVH has fewer frames than the header says.
perguntas.explica: If you redo the retargeting without redoing the check, safety is approved on one file while another one is ready to go to the robot. The check compares the file names from each step.

perguntas.p: Where does the 400°/s ceiling in the speed rule come from?
opcoes: From the official G1 spec sheet, for all joints.
It's a lab rule, and you can adjust it: there is no G1 number in the research.
From the Menagerie MJCF file, which declares the maximum speed of each joint.
From GMR, which calculates the speed ceiling from the original capture clip.
perguntas.explica: Without a manufacturer number in the training research, the course doesn't invent one: the ceiling is yours, written into the rule and adjustable with --teto-graus-s.

perguntas.p: Why does this course's tracking criterion use the gantry, while a real project's shouldn't?
opcoes: The kit does replay without a balance policy; with the policy, you measure it free-standing.
Because the gantry makes the joint error larger and easier to measure.
Because real robots always work attached to a gantry, even in production.
Because MuJoCo can't simulate free-standing robots with both hands attached.
perguntas.explica: Without the tracking policy (lesson 4), the free-standing G1 falls. In a project with mjlab or SONIC, tracking is measured without a gantry; the gantry is kept for the first test on the real robot (course 4).

itens.texto: Mocap, retargeting, tracking, and safety, always on the same file.
Limit and speed read from the motion; ceilings that are yours, written down.
Operating the real robot safely is FTH course 4.
